phases.title: See the job clearly
phases.blurb: A government post looks finished from far away. These talks are the inside: Income Tax, the exam years, and the difference between stability and a life.

phases.title: Choose a life
phases.blurb: Marriage, children, old age, and a single life, without the script that arrives the moment a salary does.

phases.title: Live more quietly
phases.blurb: Sukoon, fewer things, worry, midlife, and a normal day you can actually sit inside.

phases.title: Keep your own company
phases.blurb: What people will say, thin friendships, and a personality that does not borrow its nerve.

phases.title: A mind that is yours
phases.blurb: Festivals, phones, karma, and belief, looked at without handing the evening to a crowd.

lessons.title: सरकारी नौकरी की एक ये काली सच्चाई जरूर जान लेना। Govt job reality
lessons.note: The talk you opened. From outside, a government post looks like the dream that ends the struggle: respect, a salary, a life that is set. He says the inside story is different. Growth and promotion are slow, switching or leaving is close to impossible, and stability can turn into stagnation. The sentence he wants kept: choose work where you can still grow, not a post where you only get stuck and spend the years. This sitting starts about six minutes in, where the pretty picture gives way to that trap.
crux: A government job can look sweet from far away and tight once you are inside.
In that system, changing posts or walking out is unusually hard.
Stability and stagnation are not the same. Do not chase the label with your eyes closed.

lessons.title: Why I Left My Govt Job as an Income Tax Inspector?? Know the Truth!
lessons.note: He treats the Income Tax Inspector post as the dream millions still want, then says why he left it. The talk is his own ledger: what the job gives, what it costs, and the path after. It is not a rumor about the department. It is one officer’s ground report.
crux: The post is real security, and it is still a life he chose to leave.
Advantages and disadvantages both stay on the table.
If you are preparing, hear the inside before you give the attempt your best years.

lessons.title: Income Tax Department में Job का मेरा 5 साल का अनुभव, और मैंने क्यों छोड़ी
lessons.note: Five years inside a department people call one of the better ones, told as work rather than as a poster. What the days were like, which pressures showed up, and why the fifth year ended in an exit.
crux: The reputation of a department is not the texture of a day there.
The exit came after years, not after a bad week.
Experience is the evidence. The label is not.

lessons.title: Why I left Income Tax — Know the Reality (Part 2)
lessons.note: Part two of the same exit. He refuses the rumor version: that the system simply throws people out, or that a government job is only a dream. He tells his own story and the pressure, and asks whether these jobs are something you quit or something that slowly closes around you.
crux: Do not take the exit story from forwards. Take it from the person who left.
A prized post can still be a trap if leaving it feels impossible.
The question is not prestige. It is whether you can still move.

lessons.title: I left my job in Income Tax and chose peace
lessons.note: Respect, stability, security — he grants all three to the Income Tax job. Then he asks the missing word: peace. This is the hard decision, told as a battle inside one life, not as advice to hate every job.
crux: A respected job can still fail the peace test.
The decision was difficult because the job was actually good on paper.
Peace was the thing he chose, not a bigger designation.

lessons.title: Do I regret leaving my Income Tax Inspector job?
lessons.note: People ask the only question that matters after an exit: do you regret it? He answers with the struggle, the thinking, and what he is aiming at now. Regret is allowed in the room. It is not used as a trick to scare you back.
crux: Leaving a secure post does not end the questions. It starts the honest ones.
Regret and rightness can both be examined without a performance.
The future he describes is a direction, not a guarantee.

lessons.title: What will people say — the fear that held the exit
lessons.note: The lock on the exit was not only the salary. It was “what will people say,” and what family said first. He walks through the mental fight before he left a prestigious post.
crux: The strongest lock on a wrong-fitting life is other people’s sentences.
A family’s reaction is real. It is not the same as your life.
You can be scared and still leave.

lessons.title: The dark reality of UPSC, SSC, and banking exams
lessons.note: Is preparation the bright future, or a dream that eats the best years? He looks at why so many students sit for years and still do not arrive, and what that wait does to a life that has not started.
crux: Years of preparation are a life, not a waiting room outside life.
Most attempts do not become a post. A plan has to survive that fact.
A future that requires you to disappear until you crack it is already a cost.

lessons.title: The trap of UPSC and SSC
lessons.note: A conversation about an exam cycle that feels endless: UPSC, SSC, banking, railways. Coaching sells hope. Students run their best years without a backup, without money, and without emotional ground.
crux: An endless cycle is a product. Someone is selling the next attempt.
No backup plan is not seriousness. It is exposure.
Hope from a coaching advertisement is not a career.

lessons.title: Why I gave up UPSC preparation
lessons.note: His own UPSC years, named as a trap, a rat race, and at times an identity crisis. Why he quit, where he felt he was losing himself, and how preparation stopped being a tool and became the person.
crux: An exam can become your identity before it becomes your job.
Quitting preparation can be an escape, not a failure of nerve.
Losing yourself in the race is a result, even if you never see a result sheet.

lessons.title: UPSC has started to behave like a lottery
lessons.note: The claim in the title: at the scale the exam now runs, effort and outcome have come apart. Sit with whether your years are a craft you can trust or a ticket.
crux: When seats are tiny and the crowd is huge, hard work does not buy a result.
Calling it a lottery is a warning about odds, not an insult to people who clear it.
A life plan that depends on a lottery needs another plan beside it.

lessons.title: Five challenges after you actually get the government job
lessons.note: The post is not the ending. He names pressures that show up after joining. The dream stops at the joining letter. The job starts there.
crux: Getting the job and living the job are different chapters.
Challenges after joining are part of the contract, not a personal defect.
Ask what the fifth year looks like, not only what result day looks like.

lessons.title: The real struggle begins when the job begins
lessons.note: Before the job, the struggle is hope. After it, hope is replaced by duty, tiredness, and a slower understanding. He says the real struggle starts when the work starts.
crux: Employment does not hand you ease. It hands you a different weight.
Pre-job enthusiasm is not a preview of the office.
If you only prepared for the exam, you have not prepared for the job.

lessons.title: Are you trapped in the government-job matrix?
lessons.note: A check, not a speech against jobs. The matrix is the feeling that the post now decides your marriage, your city, your hours, and your exit. If every life question funnels back to the service, you are inside it.
crux: A matrix is a life where the job answers questions it should not own.
Feeling trapped is information. It is not disloyalty.
You can respect the work and still notice the walls.

lessons.title: Five mistakes in the first months of a career
lessons.note: The first months set habits: spending the new salary as proof that life is solved, saying yes to every duty, dropping the body, wearing the designation as a personality.
crux: The first months teach the job who you are.
A new salary is not proof that life is solved.
Avoid the mistakes while they are still small.

lessons.title: क्या बिना नौकरी जीवन नहीं चल सकता? Rat race छोड़ो
lessons.note: He is not against work. He is against the idea that a 9-to-5 is the last truth of a life, and that safety is worth pawning your freedom for. The talk is a change of mind, not a dare to quit tomorrow with no ground under you.
crux: A job can be useful without being the whole of life.
Safety that costs your freedom is a mortgage, not a gift.
Leaving the race is a strategy. It is not the same as refusing to earn.

lessons.title: Two evergreen fields for work that lasts
lessons.note: After the warnings, a practical turn. If you still want work that lasts, he points at two fields he thinks stay useful, instead of one exam that may never arrive.
crux: “Do not chase the trap” still leaves the question of how you eat.
Evergreen means the work survives a change in exam patterns.
Choose a field you can still enter if the notification never comes.

lessons.title: Stuck in the wrong job or the wrong marriage
lessons.note: Wrong work and a wrong marriage are treated as the same kind of stuck: a life you did not really choose, held in place by fear and by what society will say. He asks how you know you are in the wrong place, and why most people do not move.
crux: A wrong fit at work and at home can feel identical: you perform, you do not live.
Fear and reputation are why people stay.
Seeing that you are in the wrong place is the first honest step. It is not yet the exit.

lessons.title: Choose life, not marriage
lessons.note: The short message of the channel in one sitting. Marriage is not banned. It is refused as the automatic next chapter. The life is the thing to choose, including the possibility that marriage is not in it.
crux: A life is the decision. Marriage is one possible chapter, not the definition.
“Choose life” means you stop living as a rehearsal for a wedding.
Simple does not mean easy. It means the sentence is short enough to remember.

lessons.title: सरकारी नौकरी के बाद भी मैं शादी के ट्रैप से कैसे बचा
lessons.note: After a government job, society’s next demand is marriage. He tells a private story: the post did not protect him from that pressure, and a marriage that becomes a trap is not simple to leave. Honest, not a spectacle.
crux: A stable job makes the marriage pressure louder, not quieter.
The trap is the assumption that the next step is automatic.
Leaving that script was personal. He is not offering a stunt.

lessons.title: The costs of marriage that the speech leaves out
lessons.note: What is usually missing from the wedding speech: loss of freedom, of a private identity, of peace of mind. A warning about costs, not a claim that every marriage is a ruin.
crux: What is called the most beautiful bond can still cost you room in your own head.
The costs are practical: time, money, peace, and who gets to decide.
Hear them before the ceremony, not after.

lessons.title: शादीशुदा जीवन की कड़वी सच्चाई, और कुछ रास्ते
lessons.note: If you are already married, the tone changes. Misunderstanding, duty, the daily grind — and then practical ways to make the bond healthier. It is not only an exit lecture.
crux: Married life has ordinary pain that speeches skip.
A problem named clearly is easier to work on than pain kept vague.
Solutions are part of this sitting, not only the complaint.

lessons.title: शादी नहीं की तो शरीर और निकटता का क्या?
lessons.note: The question people use to end the conversation: if you do not marry, what about the body, and what about closeness? He treats it as a real question, then talks about living single without pretending those needs are shameful or that marriage is the only adult answer. Nothing here is a prescription for someone else’s life.
crux: The body does not disappear because you skipped a wedding.
Single can still be balanced. It asks for honesty, not a performance of purity.
The question is often a push. You can answer it without handing over your life.

lessons.title: What happens in old age if I never marry?
lessons.note: The fear of a lonely old age, examined as a fear society spreads, not as a fate already written. He takes the question apart: sorrow, pressure, and what actually takes care of a person later.
crux: “You will be alone when you are old” is a threat as often as it is a fact.
Marriage is not a guaranteed nurse for your last years.
The fear deserves a real plan, not a wedding booked to silence it.

lessons.title: Loneliness and old age, if you stay unmarried
lessons.note: A second sitting on the same fear, more on loneliness itself than on the wedding. Old age without a spouse is a problem if you have built no other company and no other care. The problem stays in view. It is not mocked.
crux: Loneliness in old age is a real risk. Marriage is not the only answer to it.
The work of company starts now, not at seventy.
Name the fear so it stops driving the decision in the dark.

lessons.title: Having children is a lifelong decision, not a symbol
lessons.note: Children are not treated as a symbol of happiness. They are a lifelong responsibility, often taken because family pressed. He speaks for a child-free life as freedom, and asks you to see the size of the decision before you make it.
crux: A child is not a mood and not a duty you owe your parents.
The cost is decades, not the first year.
Child-free is a life design. It is allowed to be deliberate.

lessons.title: India’s loneliness, and what to do with it
lessons.note: Loneliness is rising for the young and the old, including people who are married and surrounded. He looks at the risk, then at practical ways to build real connection instead of collecting company.
crux: You can be lonely in a full house. Marriage does not cancel that.
The pattern is structural, not a private failure.
Practical connection is a skill: fewer people, real, repeated.

lessons.title: How to actually enjoy a single life
lessons.note: Single is not a waiting room. The talk is about how to enjoy the days, the money, and the attention, instead of enduring them until someone arrives.
crux: A single life can be lived, not just tolerated.
Enjoyment is a practice, not the absence of a partner.
Do not pause your days for a person who is not here.

lessons.title: Breakup के बाद बाहर निकलना, EQ के पाँच बिंदु
lessons.note: Five points for the pain after a breakup, aimed at emotional steadiness rather than revenge or a rebound. The hurt is admitted. The use of it is to come out steadier, not colder.
crux: A breakup is pain. It is also information about what you can hold.
Steadiness means you stop making the pain your personality.
Five clear points beat one dramatic resolution.

lessons.title: आनंद और सुकून के साथ जीने का सूत्र
lessons.note: The calmest promise on the channel: aanand and sukoon, joy and a quiet settledness, as a formula rather than a mood you wait for. Watch it slowly. The point is a way of living an ordinary day, not a peak experience.
crux: Sukoon is built. It is not the prize after every problem is gone.
A formula you can repeat matters more than a speech you feel once.
Deep living starts in a normal day, not on a mountain.

lessons.title: कम में ज्यादा खुशी — minimalism के बिंदु
lessons.note: Minimalism as a way of thinking, not a style of empty rooms. Fewer things, more joy, some financial room, time returned, relationships less crowded by objects.
crux: Less is not deprivation if it gives you time and money back.
Here it is financial room in small steps.
Happiness tied to the next purchase is a leak.

lessons.title: A simple way through worry and anxiety
lessons.note: For the person who looks fine and is not calm. He offers a very old, very simple way of meeting worry. This is not a medical claim that anxiety vanishes. It is a practice for a mind that will not sit.
crux: Looking sorted and being calm are different.
The method is simple on purpose. Complicated comfort rarely gets used.
Worry does not leave because you earned more. It leaves by how you meet the day.

lessons.title: What people usually understand too late
lessons.note: Things he thinks school and society do not say plainly: mistakes of timing, of proving yourself, of waiting to live. A before-thirty talk that still works after.
crux: Late knowledge is still knowledge. Do not wait for a younger self.
The expensive mistakes are the ones everyone around you calls normal.
Hearing it before it costs a decade is the luck in the title.

lessons.title: 31 years, told in one sitting
lessons.note: Lessons from thirty-one years: happiness, relationships, money, career. He says they would have made the earlier years easier. Use it as a map, then return to the one lesson that actually stings.
crux: Experience compressed is useful only if you practice one piece of it.
Happiness and money are both in the talk. Neither replaces the other.
Someone else’s years can save you one repeated mistake, not your whole life.

lessons.title: From a midlife crisis to a midlife awakening
lessons.note: Feeling stuck in your thirties, forties, or fifties is framed as a chapter opening. The unease can be used, if you stop treating it as proof that you failed.
crux: A midlife crisis is often the first honest audit.
Awakening here means a new use of the years, not a new costume.
Confusion at this age is common. It is not a verdict.

lessons.title: Charvaka — happiness in this life
lessons.note: Charvaka, the old Indian materialist line: live here, in this body, in this day, without renting your joy to an afterlife. Offered as a practical key to a simpler life.
crux: Happiness that depends on another world is easy to postpone.
A this-life philosophy asks you to take the present day seriously.
Simple and enjoyable is a discipline, not shallowness.

lessons.title: Five expenses that are the opposite of a spiritual life
lessons.note: He moves spirituality off the prayer mat and onto the bill. Five large expenses that keep people stressed and mentally owned. Refusing them is, for him, the actual spiritual act.
crux: A hymn does not free you if a loan owns your month.
The expensive “musts” are often social, not sacred.
In this talk, spirituality is the art of not being enslaved by spending.

lessons.title: Five freedoms that prevent misery you do not need
lessons.note: Five freedoms, named as protection from misery that is socially supplied. While you watch, write the five in your own words and notice which one you do not have yet.
crux: A lot of misery is optional and handed to you.
Freedom here is five specific things, not a mood.
The one you cannot name is the one to sit with after the video.

lessons.title: Five formulas for a peaceful life
lessons.note: Five formulas, stated boldly in the title and worth testing rather than believing. Pair it with the sukoon talk. Formulas are for ordinary weeks.
crux: Peace is treated as repeatable, not as luck.
A formula you do not practice is a poster.
Check whether your days lack happiness, peace, or both.

lessons.title: The Titan theory of making a decision
lessons.note: A named way of deciding, so a choice stops being a crowd inside the head. Use it on one real decision you have been circling.
crux: Indecision is a cost, even when it feels like care.
A method is there so you can apply it this week.
Big decisions get worse when every voice in the room has a vote.

lessons.title: Why I quit alcohol
lessons.note: His own quitting. The early fun is admitted. Then health, money, relationships, and peace of mind leave. He gives steps that worked for him, not a lecture from someone who never drank.
crux: The early pleasure is real. So is the later bill.
Quitting is a sequence of steps, not a burst of shame.
Peace of mind is one of the things the habit spends.

lessons.title: Why so many young Indians are depressed
lessons.note: Causes he names: social media, career pressure, relationships, and the silence around it. He also talks about recognizing the signs and where to seek help. This sitting is not treatment. If you are in crisis, speak to someone beside you or a local helpline. Do not sit alone with it.
crux: Depression among the young is common and still treated as a secret.
Career pressure and the screen are part of the cause, not the whole of it.
Getting help is part of the talk. This course is not a substitute for it.

lessons.title: Suffocating at home — what the day after leaving looks like
lessons.note: Running away feels like the only door. He offers a reality check: escape looks easy, and most people have not pictured the day after. Freedom is not the same as fleeing a house with no plan.
crux: Suffocation at home is real. So is the morning after you leave.
Do not romanticize disappearance.
A clean exit needs ground: money, a place, a next week.

lessons.title: सबसे बड़ा रोग: लोग क्या कहेंगे
lessons.note: “What will people say” is named as the largest disease. It sits under the job exit, the marriage decision, and the quiet life. This talk isolates that sentence so you can hear how often it is the real boss.
crux: The sentence is not etiquette. It is a control system.
Most delayed lives are waiting for a crowd to approve.
You can be decent to people and still stop letting their sentence decide.

lessons.title: Stay away from opportunist friends and relatives
lessons.note: People who appear when you are useful and thin out when you are not. The advice is distance, not a war. The pattern shows itself when you have nothing to offer.
crux: Usefulness is not the same as friendship.
Relatives are not automatically safe.
Distance is a calm tool. Contempt is not required.

lessons.title: How to ignore people who only want a reaction
lessons.note: A rough title for a practical skill: you do not have to engage every person who wants a fight. Ignoring is treated as hygiene for a quiet mind, not as arrogance.
crux: Not every argument deserves your evening.
Ignoring is a skill when the other person wants a reaction.
Keep a standard for who gets access to your attention.

lessons.title: 500 contacts, and maybe five who stand with you
lessons.note: A full phone book is not a safety net. Quality over the size of the list, and how to tell a genuine person from a saved number.
crux: The test of a person is a hard day, not a festival.
Five real people beat five hundred names.
Stop performing for the list.

lessons.title: Four tests of a strong personality
lessons.note: Four self-tests for confidence, independence, and emotional strength. They are challenges, not a quiz score. The point is to step out of comfort and see what is actually there.
crux: Personality is what you do when it costs you, not how you introduce yourself.
Four tests beat a vague wish to be strong.
Discomfort in the test is the information.

lessons.title: The person who has learned to live alone
lessons.note: The title sounds like a threat. The talk is about friendship that has become self-interest, and about the person who no longer needs the crowd — why that independence unsettles people. Living alone is not the danger. Depending on interested friends is.
crux: A lot of modern friendship is a transaction.
People distrust the one who can stand without them.
Learn which solitude is strength and which is only a pose.

lessons.title: You are losing confidence, not hair
lessons.note: Hair loss treated as a psychological wound more than a cosmetic one. Identity and confidence get tied to hair, and that tie is the actual problem. The aim is to drop the inferiority, not to sell a cure.
crux: The mirror is often auditing your status, not your health.
Confidence lost to appearance can return without fixing the hair.
Inferiority is a story. You can stop repeating it.

lessons.title: How to help people actually see your point
lessons.note: Influence without becoming the opportunist from the earlier talks. How you present a point so another person can see it. Useful with family who only hear “what will people say.”
crux: Being right and being understood are different skills.
Force closes ears. A clear frame opens them.
Use this with people you love, not as a trick on strangers.

lessons.title: People who keep asking to borrow money
lessons.note: Money asked again and again, and money that does not come back. How to refuse, how to recover what is stuck, how to say no without burning the relationship, and when not to lend at all.
crux: A loan to a friend is often a gift you were not allowed to name.
Saying no is part of keeping the relationship.
Do not lend what you need returned in order to live.

lessons.title: Modern slavery, and the freedom on the other side of it
lessons.note: Pressure without chains: a bill for living, a bill for working, a mind that is not quite yours. He describes how the money system slowly owns an ordinary person. Listen as a map of pressure, not as a club you must join.
crux: Modern pressure does not need a jail. A monthly bill is enough.
Freedom here is economic and mental at once.
Seeing the mechanism is the start. Rage without a plan is another trap.

lessons.title: Made poorer in the name of festivals
lessons.note: The joy of a festival is real. The bill is how a year of savings leaves. He asks you to separate the rite from the shopping.
crux: A festival can be kept without the shopping that empties you.
Poverty here is manufactured in the name of belonging.
Skipping one expensive ritual is a way of staying free.

lessons.title: Festival sales, and the urgency that is not real
lessons.note: Discounts, limited time, “today or never.” Most of the sale is a story about urgency. Your wallet is the target, not your celebration.
crux: Urgency is a sales tool. It is rarely the truth about the product.
A discount on something you did not need is not savings.
Festive shopping and a poorer month can be the same evening.

lessons.title: The new phone, and who actually wanted it
lessons.note: The yearly phone as a small, visible case of the same pressure: desire made for you, labor hidden, loyalty mistaken for taste. You do not have to hate the object. You have to notice who is choosing.
crux: A new model is often an identity, not a tool.
Consumer loyalty can feel like freedom and still be a leash.
Ask who wanted it first, you or the launch.

lessons.title: “Be good and good will happen” — the karma comfort
lessons.note: The sentence we grew up with, treated as a comfort that does not match the world, where harm reaches kind people and ease reaches cruel ones. He asks what the theory explains, and what it is used to silence.
crux: Goodness is not a contract with the universe.
The theory is sometimes used to blame the person who is suffering.
Be decent because it is decent, not because a reward was promised.

lessons.title: Reason, in a country full of unasked faith
lessons.note: A strong claim for atheism against blind faith, and why he thinks soft uncertainty changes nothing. Watch it as his argument, not as an order to wear a label. The useful part is the demand that a belief survive contact with evidence.
crux: Faith that cannot be questioned will run your money and your fear.
A label is less important than the habit of checking.
You can disagree with his conclusion and still keep the demand for reason.

lessons.title: Can you sit in a temple if you do not believe?
lessons.note: Temples without God as the reason: quiet, attention, a less anxious mind. He separates the building from the belief, so a non-believer can still use the calm of the place.
crux: A temple can be a room for attention, not only a room for worship.
You do not have to believe the story to use the silence.
Know which one you are doing: ritual, or reason.

lessons.title: How much of Osho and Acharya Prashant is actually useful?
lessons.note: Two famous voices, weighed instead of followed. Where the philosophy helps, and where it becomes wordplay. He asks you to decide, not to join.
crux: A famous teacher is not a finished truth.
Enlightenment talk can be precise or it can be fog. Learn to tell them.
Keep the part that changes a Tuesday. Throw out the rest.

lessons.title: Religion, baba culture, and a meditation you can actually do
lessons.note: A long conversation with another channel: religion against spirituality, the rise of baba culture, and what an honest daily meditation looks like when it is not a performance.
crux: Spirituality that needs a crowd and a fee is worth suspecting.
Meditation in this talk is a daily practice, not a personality.
Criticism of baba culture is part of staying mentally free.

lessons.title: How much the channel has actually earned
lessons.note: After the government post, the practical question is money. This talk puts a figure on what the channel has earned, so freedom is not only a feeling. His number is not your forecast.
crux: Freedom talk without a rupee figure is incomplete.
His income is his, from his years and his audience.
Use it to see that a living can be built in public, not to copy the total.

lessons.title: Why this channel exists, and a few rules for a joyful life
lessons.note: The purpose of the channel, straight answers to comments, and plain principles for a balanced life. A last sitting: the aim is a place to think, not a pile of information.
crux: The purpose is a freer, more joyful life, not a fan club.
The principles are simple enough to use this week.
Information that does not change the day is optional.
